record.paper_title: Open Problems on Configuration Spaces of Tensegrities
record.context_brief: Cayley description of all planar codimension-one strata
record.original_question: Given a graph G, determine whether there exists one Cayley algebra system, or several such systems, that describes exactly the union of the codimension-1 tensegrity strata in the plane; equivalently, the union of the codimension-1 strata of B_2(K_n). Here a Cayley algebra system means a description built from planar points and lines using join and meet operations.

evidence.quote: Recall that the objects of (planar) Cayley algebra are points and lines in the plane. Cayley algebra has two major operations:

Problem 7 Given a graph G. Does there exist a Cayley algebra system (or several systems) describing the union of the codimension 1 tensegrity strata in the plane [i.e., the union of the codimension 1 strata of B_2(K_n)]?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Work in the real projective plane (or the affine plane with its line at infinity). The planar Cayley algebra consists of two kinds of objects, points and lines, together with two operations:
 • join: given two points, their join is the unique line through them;
 • meet: given two lines, their meet is their intersection point.
A Cayley algebra system is a finite formal expression built from a list of "free" input points and/or lines by iteratively applying join and meet; such a system, evaluated on an admissible configuration of input points, produces a finite collection of derived points and lines, and thus cuts out an algebraic condition on the input configuration (namely, that certain derived objects coincide, are collinear, are concurrent, etc.).

Tensegrity strata. Fix an integer n ≥ 2 and let K_n denote the complete graph on n labeled vertices. A planar tensegrity on K_n is a placement p = (p_1, …, p_n) of the n vertices in the plane together with a nonzero real "stress" ω_{ij} on each edge ij such that, at every vertex i, the equilibrium condition Σ_{j ≠ i} ω_{ij}(p_j − p_i) = 0 holds. For a configuration p ∈ (R^2)^n in sufficiently general position, the dimension of the space W(p) of such stresses is a function of p, and the configuration space (R^2)^n is stratified by the level sets of dim W(p) and of the sign pattern of admissible stresses. The closure of those strata where the local codimension equals 1 (i.e., the configurations p at which exactly one nontrivial linear relation among the edge stresses appears, beyond the generic value) forms the codimension-1 tensegrity stratum B_2(K_n) ⊂ (R^2)^n; denote by S_1(K_n) the union of its codimension-1 components.

Problem. Given a graph G on n vertices (and in particular for G = K_n), decide whether there exists a single Cayley algebra system, or a finite collection of Cayley algebra systems, whose simultaneous vanishing locus on (R^2)^n equals precisely S_1(K_n), the union of the codimension-1 tensegrity strata of the planar configuration space of G. Equivalently, give a Cayley-algebra (join/meet) characterization of S_1(K_n) using only the planar points p_1, …, p_n and the lines obtained from them by iterated join and meet, with no additional auxiliary points or lines allowed.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of giving a pure Cayley-algebra description of the union of codimension-1 tensegrity strata in the plane is recorded as a long-standing open problem on Cayley strata descriptions. A weaker version has been addressed using an extended Cayley algebra (with additional auxiliary elements), but it is not known whether such auxiliary elements can be eliminated, and there are candidate graphs that are suspected to provide counterexamples in the strict (non-extended) setting.
